slot.brief: Definite integral reduced by a trigonometric/half-angle substitution (e.g. sin x or tan(x/2) substitution) leading to a log or standard value.

verdicts.working: With t = tan(x/2), the integral becomes ∫₀¹ dt/(1+t) = ln 2.

working:
Set $t=\tan\dfrac{x}{2}$; then $dx=\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}$, $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$.
Limits: $t=0$ to $1$.
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x+\cos x}=\int_0^1\dfrac{dt}{1+t}=\ln 2$

Independent check: With t = tan(x/2), the integral becomes ∫₀¹ dt/(1+t) = ln 2.
solution:
Set $t=\tan\dfrac{x}{2}$, so $dx=\dfrac{2\,dt}{1+t^2}$, $\sin x=\dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}$, and $\cos x=\dfrac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$. The limits become $t=0$ to $1$.
$$\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{dx}{1+\sin x+\cos x}=\int_0^1\frac{dt}{1+t}=\ln 2.$$
